source.title: The Feature Speed Formula: a flexible approach to scale hyper-parameters of deep neural networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied. The extracted text contains minor formatting/OCR artifacts, but the relevant sections and results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper derives and numerically checks backward-feature angles and feature-update behavior during gradient descent, bearing conceptually on training dynamics and initialization. Its measures do not test the claim versions' benchmark training-error outcomes.
record.gate_note: The paper reports theoretical results and experiments on one GD step, BFA, and feature sensitivity. These do not measure training classification error, stalled training error, or the version-specific outcomes on CIFAR/ImageNet/MNIST. Cited results from other papers are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes feature-update geometry, sensitivity and instantaneous loss decay under joint initialization and learning-rate scalings. Its one-step experiments and theoretical results do not establish training speed, trainable depth, training error, local-minimum frequency, stability-threshold recovery or batch-normalization benefits named in V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors derive a feature speed formula, use backward-feature angles to characterize existing hyperparameter scalings and introduce FSC. Their conclusions concern local feature dynamics and scaling properties, rather than demonstrated end-to-end training benefits. The formula applies to (stochastic) gradient descent at architectural cut nodes and does not apply inside residual blocks.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies feature-update geometry and hyperparameter scaling, with a one-GD-step numerical measurement and theoretical large-width/depth analyses; it does not apply the benchmark training-error recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: BFA and feature sensitivity vary with architecture, depth, branch scale, and hyperparameter scaling; the text reports different asymptotic behavior for ReLU MLPs and linearly activated ResNets.

fits_no_version.finding: BFA changes across layers and branch scales in one-step ReLU MLP and ResNet experiments; the theory predicts depth-degenerate alignment in ReLU MLPs and nondegenerate alignment in suitably scaled linear ResNets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture and residual branch scaling control alignment between feature updates and the backward pass at initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: Last-hidden-layer sensitivity differs among NTK, MF+µP and FSC scalings, while the tested ResNet sensitivities remain around nonzero values.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hyperparameter scaling controls feature change per unit loss decrease at initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: Proposition 5.3 predicts instantaneous loss decay vanishing as L^−1/2 for MF+µP and remaining order one for FSC, under the stated single-input, large-width-then-depth assumptions and joint scaling of initialization and learning rates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Joint initialization and learning-rate scaling can prevent vanishing initial loss-decay rate while preserving order-one feature updates.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2024 (38th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems)
record.problems: The numerical experiments are one-GD-step measurements rather than training-error trajectories. Figure values are not numerically reported in the text. The stated large-width/depth theoretical results have architecture and assumption restrictions, including linear activation for the ResNet result.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant result rows were identified. Hyperparameter scaling properties, theoretical propositions and cited prior-work findings do not report the training classification error named by the versions.

untested.parts: Training classification error of convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels and model-size, stopping and regularization conditions.
Spurious-local-minimum frequency in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and its reduction through extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth, its prevention by identity shortcuts, and successful deep plain or normalization-free residual training.
Actual learning-speed and trainable-depth comparisons across initializations; activation-matched initialization benefits; orthogonal versus Gaussian training; and 10,000-layer convolutional training.
Recovery above the initial stability threshold, transient loss increases, curvature trajectories, edge-of-stability behavior and divergence.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparable speed and stability using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Theoretical signal propagation, gradient stability and initial loss-decay rates are related to V4 but do not establish its learning-speed or trainable-depth outcomes. The ResNet BFA theorem assumes linear activations; its ReLU extension is left open despite ReLU numerical checks. No claim-version verdicts follow from these proxy measurements.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100; random or corrupted labels; optimizer, model-size and stopping effects.
Teacher-student local minima and student-width comparisons.
Training error versus depth in plain and residual networks; shortcut and normalization comparisons; Fixup training outcomes.
Training speed and trainable depth comparisons across initializations, including orthogonal versus Gaussian and 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss trajectories, curvature and divergence outcomes.
Batch-normalization comparisons for speed, accuracy and learning-rate tolerance; Fixup outcomes.

rows.subject: MLP and ResNet models (width m = 200)
rows.operation_detail: Measured backward-feature angle at initialization across layers for a few random realizations.
rows.note: The paper describes the plot as showing BFA varies in the first few layers and then stabilizes; this is a feature-update alignment measure, not training classification error.
rows.check: BFA measures feature-update alignment, not a version's outcome. Section 5.1 specifies ReLU networks, one GD step with master learning rate 0.001, d=10, k=1 and an untrained input matrix W1; these conditions should be recorded.

rows.subject: ResNets (width m = 200)
rows.operation_detail: Measured output-layer BFA while varying depth.
rows.note: Text states output BFA is asymptotically independent of depth and has a non-trivial angle only when β ∝ 1/√L; it is not a training-error measure.
rows.check: Depth-dependent BFA cannot establish training performance. The measured index L−1 is the last hidden feature layer, although the caption calls it output BFA. Add the Section 5.1 experimental conditions specified for R1.

rows.subject: ResNets (width m = 200)
rows.operation_detail: Measured output-layer BFA while varying branch scale.
rows.measure: Output BFA θL−1 versus branch-scale factor c
rows.note: The text says c determines asymptotic output BFA; a conjectured asymptotic relation is explicitly identified as numerical conjecture.
rows.check: Branch-scale-dependent BFA cannot establish training performance. The measured index L−1 is the last hidden feature layer. The relation between c and asymptotic BFA is a numerical conjecture, not an established training result.

rows.subject: ReLU MLP
rows.operation_detail: Compared last-layer feature sensitivity for NTK, MF+µP, and FSC scalings.
rows.note: The paper reports theoretical scaling descriptions in the caption, but the plotted sensitivity is not training classification error.
rows.check: NTK sensitivity is an ancillary scaling comparison, not claim evidence. Sensitivity is feature change divided by loss change; it does not measure either training speed or final training error. Figure 2 also specifies a single input on the unit sphere.

rows.subject: ReLU MLP
rows.operation_detail: Compared last-layer feature sensitivity for NTK, MF+µP, and FSC scalings.
rows.note: The paper reports theoretical scaling descriptions in the caption, but the plotted sensitivity is not training classification error.
rows.check: MF+µP sensitivity is an ancillary scaling comparison, not claim evidence. Its depth dependence does not establish training speed or trainable depth. Figure 2 specifies a single input on the unit sphere.

rows.subject: ReLU MLP
rows.operation_detail: Compared last-layer feature sensitivity for NTK, MF+µP, and FSC scalings.
rows.note: The paper reports theoretical scaling descriptions in the caption, but the plotted sensitivity is not training classification error.
rows.check: FSC sensitivity is the proposed scaling's performance on a feature-learning criterion and should not be a claim-evidence row. Constant sensitivity does not establish faster or successful training. Figure 2 specifies a single input on the unit sphere.

rows.subject: ReLU ResNet
rows.operation_detail: Compared last-layer feature sensitivity for two branch-scale choices.

conditions.value: two choices, values not stated in caption

rows.note: The caption says sensitivities are stable around a nonzero value for both branch-scale choices; this does not measure training classification error.
rows.check: Stable nonzero sensitivity across depths and branch scales does not establish that shortcuts prevent training-error degradation. This is an ancillary feature-sensitivity experiment; Figure 2 specifies a single input on the unit sphere.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
